exact_missing_items: These three states are not synonyms and must not be conflated in any doc
Acknowledgement model: 'acknowledged' ≠ 'resolved' ≠ 'dismissed'; acknowledgement is for advisory/non-blocking concerns only; blockers are not acknowledgeable
Settings groupings must be: Providers & Models, Execution Identity, Governance, Workers, Recovery, HITL — these are the canonical top-level settings categories
GUI help/tooltip generation requires: stable canonical terminology, clear object vs state vs action distinctions, and enough 'why this exists' language to support Simple/Expert/ELI5 derivation
Concern lifecycle states must be: active, acknowledged, resolved, dismissed — in that sequence with defined allowed transitions

Governance model must define 4 execution scopes: run = full canonical graph under deterministic runtime; work package = coherent precomputed subgraph with local overseer; feature seam = cross-package oversight scope; node = smallest executable unit

Each entity type must have its own lifecycle model — there is no single universal status enum: node lifecycle, work package lifecycle, feature seam lifecycle, promotion lifecycle, worktree lane lifecycle are all distinct

Three canonical promotion classes must be defined: lane_to_package (lane result → package baseline), package_to_seam_available (package → trusted seam contribution), seam_complete (seam marked complete)
Plans/Personas.md must define overseer personas (Package Overseer, Seam Overseer) and their relation to lanes — current Personas.md only covers worker personas

Sonnet cleanup priorities: P1 = lock runtime schema anchors (add package/seam/lane/worktree/account identity + contamination/safe-point linkage); P2 = extend Glossary/Crosswalk/Decision_Policy; P3 = rebuild UI contracts around packages/seams/lanes; P4 = consolidate addenda
